security-token.shortDefinition: A digital representation of a traditional security (equity, debt, or fund share) issued on a blockchain with built-in compliance rules enforced by smart contracts.
security-token.longDefinition: Security tokens are blockchain-based digital assets that represent ownership in real-world securities such as company shares, bonds, real estate, or fund interests. Unlike utility tokens, security tokens are subject to securities regulations and must comply with laws like Reg D, Reg S, or Reg A+ in the US. They combine the benefits of traditional securities (legal rights, dividends, voting) with blockchain advantages (24/7 trading, fractional ownership, automated compliance).

kyc.shortDefinition: Regulatory process to verify the identity of clients, assess their suitability, and understand the nature of their activities to prevent fraud and money laundering.
kyc.longDefinition: Know Your Customer (KYC) is a mandatory due diligence process that financial institutions and regulated platforms must perform to verify client identities. This typically involves collecting government-issued ID, proof of address, and source of funds documentation. For security token platforms, KYC ensures only eligible investors can participate in offerings and helps maintain compliance with securities regulations.

aml.shortDefinition: Laws, regulations, and procedures designed to prevent criminals from disguising illegally obtained funds as legitimate income through financial transactions.
aml.longDefinition: Anti-Money Laundering encompasses the legal controls and corporate procedures that financial institutions must implement to detect and report suspicious activities. AML programs typically include customer due diligence, transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, and suspicious activity reporting. Blockchain-based securities platforms integrate AML checks directly into smart contracts to ensure ongoing compliance.

isin.shortDefinition: A 12-character alphanumeric code that uniquely identifies a security globally, enabling it to be held in traditional bank custody systems.
isin.longDefinition: The International Securities Identification Number is the global standard for identifying securities, administered by national numbering agencies. When a security token receives an ISIN, it can be recognized by traditional financial infrastructure including custodian banks, clearinghouses, and securities depositories. This 'TradFi bridge' enables investors to hold tokenized securities in their existing brokerage accounts.

clearstream.shortDefinition: A major international securities depository and settlement system based in Luxembourg, enabling custody and settlement of securities across 110+ markets.
clearstream.longDefinition: Clearstream Banking S.A. is one of the world's largest settlement and custody organizations, part of Deutsche Börse Group. It provides post-trade infrastructure services for domestic and international securities. Through Sails.to's TradFi bridge, security tokens can be converted to ISIN format and held in Clearstream, allowing traditional financial institutions to custody tokenized assets within their existing infrastructure.

wyoming-dao-llc.shortDefinition: A limited liability company structure recognized by Wyoming law that allows decentralized autonomous organizations to operate with legal entity status and liability protection.
wyoming-dao-llc.longDefinition: Wyoming became the first US state to legally recognize DAOs as a distinct business entity type in 2021. A Wyoming DAO LLC combines the flexibility of smart contract governance with the legal protections of a traditional LLC, including limited liability for members. This structure is ideal for tokenized securities as it provides clear legal ownership, tax treatment, and regulatory standing while enabling on-chain governance and automated operations.

series-llc.shortDefinition: A corporate structure allowing a single LLC to create multiple segregated series, each with its own assets, liabilities, and members, providing liability isolation between series.
series-llc.longDefinition: A Series LLC is a unique business structure that allows the creation of separate 'series' under one master LLC umbrella. Each series operates as a distinct entity with its own assets, liabilities, contracts, and even members, while sharing administrative overhead. For tokenized securities, this enables issuers to launch multiple offerings under one structure while maintaining complete liability separation between them.

spv.shortDefinition: A subsidiary entity created for a specific, limited purpose, typically to isolate financial risk and hold specific assets separate from a parent company.
spv.longDefinition: A Special Purpose Vehicle (also called Special Purpose Entity) is a legal entity created to fulfill a narrow, specific objective—usually to isolate assets and liabilities for financing, risk management, or regulatory purposes. In tokenized securities, SPVs are commonly used to hold underlying assets (real estate, company shares, etc.) while the tokens represent fractional ownership in the SPV, providing clear legal structure and investor protection.

accredited-investor.shortDefinition: An individual or entity meeting SEC financial thresholds ($200K+ annual income or $1M+ net worth) that qualifies to invest in unregistered securities offerings.
accredited-investor.longDefinition: Under SEC regulations, accredited investors are deemed financially sophisticated enough to understand and bear the risks of unregistered securities. Individuals qualify with annual income exceeding $200,000 ($300,000 joint) for the past two years, or net worth over $1 million excluding primary residence. Certain entities, licensed professionals, and company insiders also qualify. Most Reg D offerings are limited to accredited investors.

professional-investor.shortDefinition: Under EU/international regulations, an investor with sufficient experience, knowledge, and expertise to make independent investment decisions and assess risks.
professional-investor.longDefinition: Professional investors, as defined by MiFID II and similar international frameworks, include institutional investors (banks, funds, pension schemes), large corporations meeting asset/turnover thresholds, and individuals who opt-in based on qualitative criteria (transaction frequency, portfolio size, professional experience). Many security token offerings outside the US are structured for professional investors only to reduce regulatory burden.

reg-s.shortDefinition: SEC regulation providing a safe harbor for securities offerings made outside the United States to non-US persons, exempt from SEC registration requirements.
reg-s.longDefinition: Regulation S establishes safe harbors from SEC registration for offerings conducted entirely outside the US. To qualify, offers and sales must occur in offshore transactions with no directed selling efforts in the US. Reg S is commonly combined with Reg D offerings, allowing issuers to sell to accredited US investors under Reg D while simultaneously offering to international investors under Reg S.

reg-d.shortDefinition: SEC regulation providing exemptions from registration for private placements, allowing companies to raise capital from accredited investors without a public offering.
reg-d.longDefinition: Regulation D provides three exemption rules (504, 506(b), and 506(c)) for private securities offerings. Rule 506(b) allows unlimited capital raises from up to 35 non-accredited investors (with restrictions) and unlimited accredited investors, but prohibits general solicitation. Rule 506(c) permits general solicitation but requires all investors to be verified accredited investors. Most tokenized security offerings use 506(c) due to the public nature of blockchain.

solana.shortDefinition: A high-performance blockchain platform known for fast transaction speeds (400ms finality) and low fees, used by Sails.to for issuing security tokens.
solana.longDefinition: Solana is a Layer 1 blockchain designed for speed and scalability, capable of processing thousands of transactions per second with sub-second finality. Its low transaction costs (fractions of a cent) and fast confirmation times make it well-suited for security token operations that require frequent on-chain actions like dividend distributions, cap table updates, and compliance checks. Sails.to chose Solana for its combination of performance, cost-efficiency, and growing institutional adoption.

smart-contract.shortDefinition: Self-executing code deployed on a blockchain that automatically enforces the terms of an agreement when predetermined conditions are met.
smart-contract.longDefinition: Smart contracts are programs stored on a blockchain that run when triggered by transactions meeting specific conditions. For security tokens, smart contracts encode compliance rules (investor eligibility, transfer restrictions, holding periods), automate corporate actions (dividends, voting), and maintain the cap table. Once deployed, the rules execute automatically without intermediaries, providing transparency and reducing operational costs.

tradfi-bridge.shortDefinition: Sails.to's mechanism for converting blockchain-native security tokens to traditional ISIN securities that can be held in conventional bank custody.
tradfi-bridge.longDefinition: The TradFi (Traditional Finance) Bridge is a unique feature of Sails.to that allows investors to move between blockchain and traditional custody. Tokens held on Solana can be 'bridged' to receive an ISIN and be settled through Clearstream, appearing in the investor's regular brokerage account. Conversely, ISIN-held securities can be converted back to blockchain tokens. This hybrid approach gives investors flexibility and enables institutional adoption.

tokenization.shortDefinition: The process of converting ownership rights in an asset into digital tokens on a blockchain, enabling fractional ownership and programmable compliance.
tokenization.longDefinition: Tokenization transforms traditional assets—real estate, company equity, art, funds—into digital tokens representing fractional ownership shares. Each token is backed by the underlying asset and carries legal rights (dividends, voting, proceeds). Blockchain tokenization enables 24/7 trading, instant settlement, fractional ownership in small denominations, automated compliance, and global accessibility while maintaining regulatory compliance.

custody.shortDefinition: The safekeeping and administration of securities on behalf of investors, including settlement, corporate actions processing, and record-keeping.
custody.longDefinition: Securities custody involves holding assets safely on behalf of clients and handling administrative duties like dividend collection, proxy voting, and corporate action processing. Sails.to offers hybrid custody: tokens can be self-custodied in Solana wallets or held in qualified custody through the ISIN/Clearstream bridge. This flexibility allows investors to choose between DeFi-style control and TradFi-style institutional services.

secondary-trading.shortDefinition: The buying and selling of securities after their initial issuance, providing liquidity and price discovery for investors seeking to exit positions.
secondary-trading.longDefinition: Secondary trading occurs when investors trade previously issued securities among themselves, rather than buying directly from the issuer. For tokenized securities, secondary markets can operate 24/7 on blockchain-based exchanges, with smart contracts automatically enforcing transfer restrictions and compliance. Sails.to's broker network facilitates compliant secondary trading, matching buyers with sellers while ensuring all parties meet eligibility requirements.

cap-table.shortDefinition: A complete record of a company's securities ownership, showing all shareholders, their holdings, and ownership percentages, updated in real-time on blockchain.
cap-table.longDefinition: A capitalization table tracks who owns what percentage of a company or fund, including all equity classes, convertible instruments, and option pools. Traditional cap tables are maintained in spreadsheets prone to errors. Blockchain-based cap tables update automatically with every token transfer, providing a single source of truth that's always accurate, auditable, and accessible to authorized parties.

distributions.shortDefinition: Payments made to security token holders, including dividends, interest, rental income, or liquidation proceeds, automated via smart contracts.
distributions.longDefinition: Distributions are payments from issuers to token holders, representing their share of profits, income, or proceeds. On Sails.to, distributions are automated through smart contracts: when an issuer initiates a distribution, the system calculates each holder's share based on the real-time cap table and executes payments directly to their wallets (or traditional accounts for ISIN holders). This eliminates intermediaries and ensures instant, error-free dividend processing.

coupon.shortDefinition: The periodic interest payment made to bondholders, typically expressed as an annual percentage of the bond's nominal value.
coupon.longDefinition: A coupon (also known as the coupon rate or interest rate) is the annual interest payment that a bond issuer agrees to pay bondholders. It is expressed as a percentage of the bond's nominal (face) value and determines the periodic cash flows the bondholder will receive. For example, a bond with a €1,000 nominal value and a 6% coupon pays €60 per year in interest.

maturity.shortDefinition: The date on which a bond's principal amount becomes due and payable to the bondholder.
maturity.longDefinition: Maturity refers to the specific date when a debt instrument's principal (face value) must be repaid to the investor. At maturity, bondholders receive their original investment back plus any final interest payment. Bond terms can range from short-term (under 1 year) to long-term (30+ years). The maturity date, combined with coupon rate and current price, determines a bond's yield.

nominal-value.shortDefinition: The face value of a security as stated by the issuer, representing the principal amount for bonds or stated value per share for equity.
nominal-value.longDefinition: Nominal value (also called face value or par value) is the stated value of a security as declared by the issuer. For bonds, it represents the amount that will be repaid at maturity. For equity, it's the minimum legal value assigned to each share. CrossSecurities bonds typically have a nominal value that determines the coupon payments and redemption amount.

soft-cap.shortDefinition: The minimum funding threshold an offering must reach for the capital raise to proceed. If the soft cap is not met, investor funds are typically returned.
soft-cap.longDefinition: A soft cap is the minimum amount of capital an issuer must raise for a securities offering to be considered successful. If the soft cap is not reached by the offering deadline, the raise is typically cancelled and all investor funds are returned in full. On Sails.to, investor funds are held in escrow until the soft cap is reached, protecting investors from committing capital to underfunded offerings.

trustee.shortDefinition: An independent fiduciary entity that represents and protects the interests of bondholders or investors, ensuring issuers meet their obligations.
trustee.longDefinition: A trustee is an independent party (typically a regulated financial institution) appointed to represent the collective interests of bondholders or other security holders. The trustee monitors the issuer's compliance with bond covenants, holds collateral on behalf of investors, and can take action to protect investor rights if the issuer defaults. For CrossSecurities, the trustee ensures continuity of investor protections regardless of holding form.

otc.shortDefinition: Securities trading conducted directly between two parties without a centralized exchange, facilitated through a network of licensed brokers.
otc.longDefinition: Over-the-counter (OTC) trading refers to securities transactions conducted directly between two parties, rather than through a centralized exchange. OTC markets offer flexibility for trading less liquid securities and allow for negotiated terms. Sails.to's multi-broker OTC network facilitates compliant secondary trading of CrossSecurities with atomic settlement on Solana.

broker-dealer.shortDefinition: A licensed securities professional who can execute trades and place investors in CrossSecurities offerings through the Sails.to network.
broker-dealer.longDefinition: A broker-dealer is a regulated financial professional or firm licensed to buy and sell securities on behalf of clients (broker function) and for their own account (dealer function). On Sails.to, broker-dealers can participate in the multi-broker network to distribute offerings, facilitate secondary trading, and provide liquidity to investors while ensuring regulatory compliance.

liquidity.shortDefinition: The ease of buying or selling a security without significantly affecting its price — provided for CrossSecurities through the multi-broker OTC network.
liquidity.longDefinition: Liquidity measures how quickly and easily an asset can be converted to cash without a significant price discount. High liquidity means many buyers and sellers, tight bid-ask spreads, and minimal price impact. Sails.to's multi-broker OTC network enhances liquidity for CrossSecurities by connecting multiple market makers and enabling cross-broker trading with atomic settlement.

crosssecurities.shortDefinition: Securities that can be held on-chain or via traditional bank/brokerage custody — and crossed from one form to another at will.
crosssecurities.longDefinition: Sails CrossSecurities are a new class of securities that exist simultaneously in blockchain and traditional finance formats. Investors can hold them on-chain on Solana with direct wallet custody, or CrossConvert them to bankable ISIN form held via Clearstream. This hybrid approach combines DeFi benefits (instant settlement, programmable compliance) with TradFi compatibility (bank custody, brokerage integration).

on-chain.shortDefinition: Recorded directly on a blockchain — CrossSecurities exist on-chain on Solana with ownership, transfers, and compliance enforced by smart contracts.
on-chain.longDefinition: On-chain refers to data and transactions that are recorded directly on a blockchain, providing immutability, transparency, and programmatic enforcement. For CrossSecurities, on-chain holdings mean tokens exist in the investor's Solana wallet with ownership verified by the blockchain, transfers executed via smart contracts, and compliance rules automatically enforced.

bankable.shortDefinition: Securities in a format recognized by traditional banking infrastructure — CrossSecurities can CrossConvert to bankable ISIN form held via Clearstream.
bankable.longDefinition: Bankable refers to securities that can be held and processed by traditional banking and brokerage infrastructure. CrossSecurities achieve bankable status through CrossConversion to ISIN format, enabling settlement via Clearstream and custody through conventional financial institutions. This allows institutional investors to hold tokenized assets within their existing operational frameworks.

crossconversion.shortDefinition: The process of moving Sails CrossSecurities between on-chain and bankable forms while maintaining 1:1 backing.
crossconversion.longDefinition: CrossConversion is Sails.to's proprietary mechanism for converting securities between blockchain and traditional formats. Tokens held on Solana can be CrossConverted to bankable ISIN form held via Clearstream, and vice versa. The process maintains 1:1 backing — tokens are burned when converted to ISIN and minted when converted back — ensuring total supply integrity across both formats.

vienna-mtf.shortDefinition: A regulated Multilateral Trading Facility providing compliant secondary trading for security tokens and traditional securities.
vienna-mtf.longDefinition: Vienna MTF is a regulated multilateral trading facility that enables compliant secondary market trading for security tokens alongside traditional securities. As a licensed venue under EU financial regulations, it provides a regulated environment for price discovery and liquidity. CrossSecurities in bankable form can be traded on Vienna MTF, offering investors an additional liquidity venue.

compliance.shortDefinition: Adherence to legal, regulatory, and internal requirements — automated and enforced on-chain for CrossSecurities through KYC/AML, investor eligibility, and transfer restrictions.
compliance.longDefinition: Compliance encompasses all activities ensuring adherence to applicable laws, regulations, and internal policies. For CrossSecurities, compliance is automated through smart contracts that enforce investor eligibility (KYC/AML verification, accreditation status), transfer restrictions (lock-up periods, investor limits), and regulatory reporting. This programmable compliance reduces operational burden while maintaining regulatory standing.

investor-verification.shortDefinition: The process of confirming an investor's identity, financial status, and eligibility to participate in private securities offerings.
investor-verification.longDefinition: Investor verification is the comprehensive process of confirming that potential investors meet all requirements to participate in a securities offering. This includes identity verification (KYC), anti-money laundering checks (AML), accreditation or professional investor status verification, and suitability assessment. On Sails.to, verification is completed once and enables investment across all platform offerings.

brokerage-fee.shortDefinition: A fee charged by a broker for executing securities transactions on behalf of clients, typically a percentage of transaction value.
brokerage-fee.longDefinition: Brokerage fees are charges levied by broker-dealers for executing buy or sell orders on behalf of clients. In secondary trading of CrossSecurities, brokerage fees compensate brokers for matching counterparties, ensuring compliance, and facilitating atomic settlement. Fee structures vary by broker and may be fixed amounts or percentages of transaction value.

distribution-fee.shortDefinition: A fee charged for placing investors in a primary securities offering, compensating brokers and platforms for distribution services.
distribution-fee.longDefinition: Distribution fees are charges for placing investors during the primary offering of securities. These fees compensate broker-dealers and platforms for investor outreach, due diligence support, subscription processing, and compliance. On Sails.to, distribution fees are success-based, meaning issuers only pay when capital is successfully raised.

atomic-settlement.shortDefinition: A transaction mechanism where all parts of a trade execute simultaneously and completely, or not at all — eliminating settlement risk.
atomic-settlement.longDefinition: Atomic settlement is a blockchain-native feature ensuring that all components of a transaction complete simultaneously or none complete at all. For CrossSecurities trading, this means token delivery and payment happen in the same transaction block — eliminating the counterparty risk inherent in traditional T+2 settlement. If any part fails, the entire transaction reverts.

offering-memorandum.shortDefinition: Legal document detailing investment terms, risks, use of proceeds, and issuer information — required for all CrossSecurities offerings on Sails.to.
offering-memorandum.longDefinition: An offering memorandum (also called private placement memorandum or PPM) is the comprehensive legal disclosure document provided to potential investors in a private securities offering. It details the investment opportunity, terms, risks, use of proceeds, issuer background, and legal structure. All CrossSecurities offerings require a complete offering memorandum reviewed for regulatory compliance.

private-placement.shortDefinition: Sale of securities directly to qualified investors without public offering registration — the primary method for issuing CrossSecurities on Sails.to.
private-placement.longDefinition: A private placement is a securities offering sold directly to a limited number of qualified investors rather than through a public offering. This approach allows issuers to raise capital without the cost and disclosure requirements of public registration, under exemptions like Reg D (US) and Reg S (international). Most CrossSecurities are issued through private placement structures.

commission.shortDefinition: Fees paid to brokers and introducers for placing investors or facilitating trades — typically a percentage of the investment or transaction value.
commission.longDefinition: Commissions are fees paid to intermediaries (brokers, introducers, placement agents) for their role in bringing investors to an offering or facilitating trades. Commission structures vary but are typically expressed as a percentage of capital placed or transaction value. Sails.to's transparent fee structure ensures all parties understand commission arrangements upfront.

hard-cap.shortDefinition: The maximum amount of capital an issuer will accept in a securities offering, enforced automatically by smart contracts.
hard-cap.longDefinition: A hard cap is the absolute maximum amount of capital an issuer will raise in a securities offering. Once reached, no additional investments are accepted. On Sails.to, hard caps are enforced automatically by smart contracts — when the cap is reached, subscription transactions are rejected. This ensures issuers don't over-dilute and investors have certainty about total raise size.

minimum-investment.shortDefinition: $150,000 minimum investment threshold for CrossSecurities — set to comply with professional and accredited investor regulations globally.
minimum-investment.longDefinition: The minimum investment is the smallest amount an investor can commit to a securities offering. For CrossSecurities, the $150,000 minimum ensures compliance with professional investor thresholds across multiple jurisdictions and reflects the target investor base of qualified, sophisticated investors. This threshold helps maintain regulatory compliance under Reg D, Reg S, and MiFID II frameworks.

security-deposit.shortDefinition: An upfront payment required from issuers to initiate onboarding and cover preliminary structuring costs on Sails.to.
security-deposit.longDefinition: A security deposit is a refundable or partially refundable payment required from issuers at the beginning of the onboarding process. It covers preliminary costs for legal structuring, compliance review, and platform setup. The deposit demonstrates issuer commitment and is typically credited against success fees when the offering completes successfully.

operating-series.shortDefinition: A dedicated series within a Series LLC structure that holds an issuer's specific project assets and liabilities, isolating them from other offerings.
operating-series.longDefinition: An operating series is a segregated cell within a Series LLC structure that holds the assets, liabilities, and operations of a specific project or offering. Each issuer on Sails.to receives their own operating series under the Wyoming DAO Series LLC, providing complete liability isolation from other issuers while sharing administrative infrastructure.

treasury-series.shortDefinition: A dedicated series within a Series LLC structure that holds un-issued or repurchased tokens, managing token supply.
treasury-series.longDefinition: A treasury series is a segregated cell within the Series LLC structure that holds tokens not yet distributed to investors or tokens that have been repurchased. This series manages token supply, facilitates corporate actions, and provides a mechanism for issuers to maintain or adjust their capital structure over time.

crossconversion-series.shortDefinition: A dedicated series that facilitates conversion of securities between on-chain tokens and bankable ISIN format, maintaining 1:1 backing.
crossconversion-series.longDefinition: The CrossConversion series is a specialized cell within the Series LLC structure that manages the conversion of securities between on-chain and bankable formats. It holds the backing for both token forms, ensuring 1:1 correspondence between total on-chain tokens and total ISIN-held securities. This series enables the seamless CrossConversion that makes CrossSecurities unique.

escrow.shortDefinition: A neutral holding arrangement where investor funds are held by a trusted third party until predetermined conditions (like soft cap) are met.
escrow.longDefinition: Escrow is a financial arrangement where funds are held by a neutral third party until specific conditions are satisfied. For CrossSecurities offerings, investor funds are held in escrow until the soft cap is reached. If the offering fails to meet its soft cap, escrowed funds are returned to investors automatically. This protects investors from committing capital to unsuccessful raises.

operational-trust.shortDefinition: A trust structure used to hold and manage operational assets on behalf of investors, providing independent oversight and administration.
operational-trust.longDefinition: An operational trust is a legal arrangement where assets are held and managed by an independent trustee for the benefit of investors. This structure provides additional governance and protection beyond corporate structures, with the trustee having fiduciary duties to act in investors' best interests. Operational trusts may be used for specific asset classes or jurisdictional requirements.

bloom.shortDefinition: The application engine layer of Sails.to, built on Sandstorm/Melusina OS, providing the grain runtime for all platform applications.
bloom.longDefinition: BLOOM is the application engine that powers all user-facing and backend services on the Sails.to platform. Built on top of the Sandstorm/Melusina OS grain runtime, it provides isolated, capability-secured application instances for every platform function — from offerings and cap tables to compliance checks and investor portals.

cap-n-proto.shortDefinition: A zero-copy serialization protocol used for inter-grain RPC in the Sails.to platform, eliminating encoding/decoding overhead.
cap-n-proto.longDefinition: Cap'n Proto is a high-performance serialization and RPC framework that enables zero-copy data exchange between grains in the Sandstorm/Melusina OS runtime. Unlike JSON or Protocol Buffers, data is stored in its wire format, eliminating serialization costs entirely. Sails.to uses Cap'n Proto for all inter-grain communication, ensuring minimal latency between platform services.

grain.shortDefinition: The fundamental isolation unit in Sandstorm/Melusina OS — a sandboxed application instance with its own storage, capabilities, and lifecycle.
grain.longDefinition: A grain is the core abstraction in the Sandstorm/Melusina OS runtime. Each grain is a fully isolated application instance running in its own Linux container with dedicated storage, journal state, and capability references. Grains communicate exclusively through Cap'n Proto RPC and the Powerbox capability system, ensuring no unauthorized data sharing between platform services.

management-fee.shortDefinition: An ongoing fee charged for the administration and management of a securities offering. Sails.to operates on a success-based model with no upfront management fees.
management-fee.longDefinition: A management fee is a periodic charge levied by an asset manager or platform operator for ongoing portfolio administration, compliance monitoring, and investor services. In traditional finance, management fees typically range from 0.5% to 2% annually. Sails.to differentiates by operating on a success-based distribution fee model rather than charging upfront management fees.

master-nft.shortDefinition: The root authority token in Sails.to's 4-layer NFT hierarchy on Solana, controlled by 3-of-5 keyholder threshold signing.
master-nft.longDefinition: The Master NFT sits at the apex of Sails.to's on-chain authority structure on Solana. It is the only token with the authority to mint Reseller NFTs, and its transfer or modification requires 3-of-5 threshold signatures from designated keyholders. This design ensures that no single party can unilaterally control platform-level operations.

melusina.shortDefinition: The on-chain authority layer for Sails.to — a Solana-based system implementing NFT hierarchies, KYC credentialing, SPL-2022 compliance tokens, and threshold crypto.
melusina.longDefinition: Melusina is both the on-chain authority protocol and the sovereign operating system powering Sails.to. On Solana, it implements the NFT hierarchy (Master → Reseller → License → Share), Transfer Hook compliance enforcement, and threshold-signed governance. Off-chain, Melusina OS provides the sandboxed grain runtime where all platform applications execute in isolation.

nft-hierarchy.shortDefinition: Sails.to's 4-layer authority structure on Solana: Master NFT → Reseller NFT → License NFT (pNFT) → Share NFT, ensuring cryptographic chain of trust.
nft-hierarchy.longDefinition: The NFT Hierarchy is the on-chain governance architecture for Sails.to on Solana. It consists of four layers: the Master NFT (platform root authority), Reseller NFTs (broker-dealer authorization), License NFTs (programmable NFTs authorizing specific offering issuance), and Share NFTs (the actual investor-held security tokens). Each layer can only be minted by its parent, creating an immutable chain of trust.

offering.shortDefinition: A structured securities fundraise on Sails.to, governed by an Offering Grain with its own token supply, compliance configuration, and distribution waterfall.
offering.longDefinition: An offering on Sails.to is a fully configured securities issuance backed by a dedicated Offering Grain. Each offering specifies its own token parameters (supply, nominal value, currency), compliance rules (investor eligibility, jurisdictional restrictions), distribution waterfall, and cap table. Offerings can be structured as Reg D (US accredited), Reg S (non-US), or dual-exempt placements.

paying-agent.shortDefinition: The entity authorized to execute distributions and manage the revenue waterfall for a Sails.to offering, operating under Trustee oversight.
paying-agent.longDefinition: A paying agent is the designated entity responsible for executing dividend and coupon payments to investors in a Sails.to offering. The paying agent operates under the supervision of the Trustee and follows the pre-defined waterfall structure to ensure distributions are made in the correct priority order. On-chain, paying agent actions are enforced through smart contract logic.

pda.shortDefinition: A deterministic Solana account address derived from program seeds, used in Sails.to for trustless, programmatic state management.
pda.longDefinition: Program Derived Addresses (PDAs) are special Solana accounts whose addresses are deterministically computed from a set of seeds and a program ID. Unlike regular accounts, PDAs have no private key — only the owning program can sign for them. Sails.to uses PDAs extensively to store offering state, investor records, and compliance data in a trustless, verifiable manner.

powerbox.shortDefinition: The inter-grain capability sharing mechanism in Sandstorm/Melusina OS, enabling secure permission delegation via claim tokens and persistent sturdyRefs.
powerbox.longDefinition: The Powerbox is the capability brokering system in Sandstorm/Melusina OS that allows grains to share resources and permissions without direct coupling. When a grain needs access to another grain's functionality, it requests a capability through the Powerbox, which mediates the handshake and issues a persistent sturdyRef. This ensures all inter-grain access is explicitly authorized and auditable.

sandstorm.shortDefinition: An open-source platform for self-hosting web applications, providing OS-level isolation for each application instance (grain) in the Sails.to runtime.
sandstorm.longDefinition: Sandstorm is the open-source self-hosting platform that forms the foundation of Melusina OS. It provides Linux container-based isolation for every application instance (grain), automatic HTTPS, capability-based access control, and data portability. Sails.to builds on Sandstorm to deliver a sovereign runtime where all platform services — from offerings to compliance — run in isolated grains.

threshold-signing.shortDefinition: M-of-N keyholder cryptographic operations used to protect critical Sails.to platform actions, implementing distributed authority on Solana.
threshold-signing.longDefinition: Threshold signing is a cryptographic scheme where M out of N designated keyholders must cooperate to produce a valid signature. Sails.to uses 3-of-5 threshold signing for Master NFT operations, ensuring no single party can unilaterally execute platform-level actions such as minting new Reseller NFTs or modifying compliance parameters.

transfer-hook.shortDefinition: A Solana SPL-2022 extension that intercepts token transfers and enforces compliance rules before allowing any transfer to proceed.
transfer-hook.longDefinition: The Transfer Hook is a Solana SPL-2022 token extension that enables Sails.to to enforce compliance at the protocol level. Every token transfer triggers the hook program, which checks investor KYC status, jurisdictional eligibility, lock-up periods, and transfer restrictions before allowing the transaction to complete. If any check fails, the transfer reverts atomically.

waterfall.shortDefinition: The revenue distribution priority structure for Sails.to offerings, enforcing investor-first payment order on-chain via smart contracts.
waterfall.longDefinition: A waterfall is the contractual priority sequence in which revenues from a Sails.to offering are distributed. Typically, the waterfall ensures that investor distributions (coupons, dividends) are paid first, followed by platform fees, management fees, and residual distributions. On Sails.to, the waterfall is enforced on-chain through the Distribution Grain and smart contract logic.

white-label.shortDefinition: Branded platform instances available to regulated institutions, trust companies, and broker-dealers, with custom theming and compliance configuration.
white-label.longDefinition: White-label deployments allow regulated institutions (broker-dealers, trust companies, fund administrators) to operate their own branded instance of the Sails.to platform. Each white-label deployment includes custom theming, domain configuration, dedicated compliance rules, and isolated data storage, while sharing the same underlying infrastructure and code updates.
